_meta.indication: BRIDION is indicated for the reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium bromide and vecuronium bromide in adults undergoing surgery.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized study in Europe comparing rocuronium or vecuronium reversal with sugammadex 2 mg/kg vs neostigmine in a 'shallow' neuromuscular block scenario (return of T2)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults undergoing surgery requiring reversal of rocuronium- or vecuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade at shallow block (reappearance of T2)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to recovery of the train-of-four ratio T4/T1 = 0.9
pivotal_trials.result: Sugammadex provided faster recovery to T4/T1=0.9: 1:29 (rocuronium) vs 18:30 for comparator; p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.design: United States study comparing rocuronium or vecuronium reversal with sugammadex 4 mg/kg vs neostigmine in a 'profound' neuromuscular block scenario (1-2 post-tetanic counts)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults requiring reversal of rocuronium- or vecuronium-induced profound neuromuscular blockade (1-2 post-tetanic contractions)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to recovery of the train-of-four ratio T4/T1 = 0.9
pivotal_trials.result: Sugammadex 4 mg/kg provided faster recovery: 2:52 (rocuronium) vs 50:22 for comparator; p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.design: United States and Canada study of immediate reversal: sugammadex 16 mg/kg at 3 minutes following rocuronium vs succinylcholine with no reversal agent
pivotal_trials.population: Adults requiring immediate reversal of a rapid sequence induction dose of rocuronium (1.2 mg/kg) at three minutes
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Return of T1 in a TOF stimulus to 10% of baseline (T1 = 0.1)
pivotal_trials.result: Sugammadex reversed blockade faster than succinylcholine spontaneous recovery: 4:22 vs 7:04; p<0.0001 (reported as 4.3 vs 7.2 minutes on average)

pivotal_trials.design: Europe study of 'shallow' neuromuscular block (return of T2) comparing rocuronium/sugammadex 2 mg/kg vs cis-atracurium/neostigmine
pivotal_trials.population: Adults requiring reversal of rocuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade at shallow block (reappearance of T2)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to recovery of the train-of-four ratio T4/T1 = 0.9
pivotal_trials.result: Sugammadex 2 mg/kg provided faster recovery: 2:02 vs 8:46 for comparator; p<0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and higher than placebo): vomiting, pain, nausea, hypotension, and headache. In pooled Phase 1-3 studies at 4 mg/kg, nausea occurred in 26%, pain in 52%, and vomiting in 12%. Serious risks include anaphylaxis (0.3% of healthy volunteers) and marked bradycardia, some resulting in cardiac arrest.
target_moa: Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin, a selective relaxant binding agent that forms a 1:1 complex encapsulating rocuronium or vecuronium, thereby reversing their neuromuscular blockade.

advisory_committee.vote: Presented to the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee (AADPAC) on November 6, 2015; the committee voted 14 Yes / 0 No that the efficacy, safety and overall risk-benefit profile support approval.

description.text: Added use in pediatric patients ages 2 to less than 17 years for reversal of neuromuscular blockade

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes changes to the Package Insert based on data to fulfill the requirements of postmarketing requirement (PMR) 3003-8 in pediatric patients ages 2 to less than 17 years old. The data is from Study P089 - A Phase 4 Double-Blinded, Randomized, Active Comparator-Controlled Clinical Trial to Study the Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics of Sugammadex (MK-8616) for Reversal of Neuromuscular Blockade in Pediatric Participants.

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients from birth to less than 2 years of age for reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium

citations.quote: Bridion (sugammadex) injection is now approved for use in pediatric patients ages from birth to less than 2 years old for reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium bromide and vecuronium bromide. This supplement provides for pediatric information pursuant to both the Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) and the Pediatric Research Act (PREA). This approval is in response to both a Written Request and a PREA PMR.

summary.text: BRIDION (sugammadex), a new molecular entity gamma-cyclodextrin, was submitted under section 505(b) with original receipt October 31, 2007. It underwent a protracted regulatory history — a Not Approvable letter (July 31, 2008) and a Complete Response letter (September 20, 2013) — and was presented to the AADPAC advisory committee on November 6, 2015 before being approved in December 2015 for reversal of rocuronium/vecuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade in adults undergoing surgery, with required postmarketing studies.

citations.quote: submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for BRIDION (sugammadex) Injection, 100 mg/mL.

Sugammadex, also known as Org25969, is a new molecular entity of the \gamma-cyclodextrin class. It was designed, by selective addition of functional groups around the structure, to bind rocuronium and vecuronium.

requirement.text: 3003-1: Required deferred pediatric study (PREA) — a randomized controlled trial evaluating efficacy, safety and PK of sugammadex for reversing rocuronium- or vecuronium-induced neuromuscular blockade in pediatric patients birth to 17 years old.

citations.quote: 3003-1 A randomized, controlled trial evaluating the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of sugammadex injection when used to reverse neuromuscular blockade induced by either rocuronium or vecuronium must be conducted in pediatric patients ages birth to 17 years old.

requirement.text: 3003-2: Conduct a postmarketing study to characterize the demographics, concomitant medications, and comorbidities of patients who did not respond to sugammadex reversal, to determine the profile of expected non-responders.

citations.quote: 3003-2 Conduct a postmarketing study to analyze the demographic characteristics, concomitant medication use, and comorbid conditions in patients who did not respond to sugammadex reversal in the development program, in postmarket studies that have been conducted, or as described in cases of non-response/lack of efficacy reported as postmarketing adverse events.

requirement.text: 3003-3: Conduct a postmarketing clinical trial comparing sugammadex to placebo and/or approved reversal drugs in ASA Class 3 and 4 patients to characterize the risks of bradycardia and other cardiac arrhythmias.

citations.quote: 3003-3 Conduct a postmarketing clinical trial comparing sugammadex to placebo and/or drugs approved for the management of the reversal of the effects of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium in a population of American Society of Anesthesiologists Class 3 and 4 patients.

requirement.text: 3003-4: Conduct a postmarketing clinical trial comparing sugammadex to placebo and/or approved reversal drugs in patients with morbid obesity to evaluate safety and support dosing recommendations.

citations.quote: 3003-4 Conduct a postmarketing clinical trial comparing sugammadex to placebo and/or drugs approved for the management of the reversal of the effects of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium in patients with morbid obesity.

citations.quote: However, the observations from the routine inspections indicated several protocol violations that raised questions about the integrity and reliability of the data generated from Study P101, the key study intended to address the remaining deficiency.
